newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber ends sharply higher, Nov up $10 limit.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber ends sharply higher, Nov up $10 limit.

text.p: CME lumber futures closed sharply higher in nearby contracts and November was up the $10-per-tbf daily limit in reaction to strong demand for cash lumber by home builders, traders said.

Lumber dealers let inventories run low this summer in anticipation of lower lumber prices. Instead prices stayed firm and an unusual late-season building surge had dealers scrambling for wood to supply builders.
"It's a little better market that what some people had expected," said Neil Schmaedick, a forest products analyst with Smith Barney.
Because of the building demand, lumber mills have been commanding high prices for their production. "The mills are the only ones who have supplies right now," said Schmaedick.
On Friday, Random Lengths quoted cash spruce at $422 per thousand board feet up from $414 a week earlier. Also, Random Lengths' framing lumber price index was $451 Friday versus $349 a year ago.
Schmaedick said demand should keep cash spruce trading from $420 to $425 the next few weeks.
Lumber closed up $10.00 to $6.10 per tbf with September up $8.60 at $422.80 per tbf and November was limit up at $378.30.
